   MINUTES OF TUESDAY, JULY 26, 2022
  MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  HUMAN EQUITY, ACCESS, AND RELATIONS (HEAR) COMMISSION

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Jennings-Nuñez called the regular meeting of the HEAR Commission to order at 6:32 p.m.
on Tuesday, July 26, 2022, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San
Gabriel, California, 91776.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Vice Chair Goto.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Michelle Brenhaug, Jacqueline Borja, Susan Fitzsimmons, Viki Goto,
  Jorge Herrera, Chasity Jennings-Nuñez, and Riaz (Rick) Khan

Commissioners Absent:  All commissioners present.

ANNOUNCMENTS

Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager, provided information for the public on
how to submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the HEAR
Commission, e-mail all public comments to HEARCommission@sgch.org.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez hearing no objections, the Agenda Order was approved.

  2. PUBLIC COMMENT

  None

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  JULY 26, 2022
   3. ACTION ITEMS

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The Commission commented on a couple grammatical errors on the June minutes.

  A motion was made by Vice Chair Goto and seconded by Commissioner Khan to
  approve the revised minutes of the HEAR Commission Regular Meeting for June
  28, 2022.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 7-0-0 as follows:
  Ayes: Brenhaug, Borja, Fitzsimmons, Goto, Herrera, Jennings-Nuñez, Khan
  Nays: None
  Abstain: None

  4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. GUEST SPEAKER – CHERYL SHELLHART
  Chair Jennings-Nuñez introduced the guest speaker.

  Cheryl Shellheart with the San Gabriel Valley Special Needs Group provided a
  presentation regarding the services and programs her community-based
  organization offers to San Gabriel residents and the surrounding communities.
  These services include monthly parent support group meetings, parent education
  meetings and classes and scholarships to deserving seniors. They also provide
  gift cards to special education elementary school teachers for supplies.

  The Commission thanked Ms. Shellhart for the presentation and commended her
  for all her hard work and passion. They inquired about the number of
  participants and how the families are recruited. They asked if the program was
  available to everyone or just San Gabriel residents. The Commission also had
  questions regarding the first steps parents can take to help their child. Chair
  Jennings- Nuñez asked if the organization would be interested in providing a
  presentation with the police department to enhance interactions with persons
  with learning differences.

  Public Comment: None

  The Commission took a short health break, the meeting resumed at 7:16 p.m.

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  JULY 26, 2022
   B. DISCUSSION OF APPROVED 2022 ANNUAL WORKPLAN

  Commissioner Brenhaug provided an update regarding the San Gabriel Mental
  Wellness Expo. There will be 3 different workshops in three languages, English,
  Mandarin, and Spanish. These workshops will be provided by the LA County
  Department of Mental Health and will cover anxiety disorder, grief & loss, and
  childhood anxiety & depression. The Commission discussed the location logistics
  of the workshops and presentations, made edits to the event flyer, spoke about
  registration and food options. They also mentioned giveaways, potential donors,
  donations and adding components such as Tai Chi or Yoga. Chair Jennings-Nuñez
  shared information about a grant provided by the San Gabriel Community
  Foundation that could help support this program.

  HEAR Commission will have a booth at National Night Out on August 2nd.

  The next guest speaker for the August meeting will be the LA County Recorder/
  Clerk’s office. They will be providing election information. The September meeting
  speaker is Nora Maldonado LA County Department of Mental Health. Elio Lopez
  from Foothill Family Clinic will speak at the meeting in October. There will be no
  speakers in November or December.

  The Commission spoke about the police department and data collection. City
  Manager Lazaretto provided clarification regarding Assembly Bill 481.

  Commissioner Borja provided an update regarding the Youth Engagement Survey.
  The survey will be included in the drive-by backpack giveaway hosted by ICNA
  Relief and Mosque in conjunction with the school district on July 28. The survey
  will also be shared at National Night Out and another city backpack giveaway
  event.

  The Commission asked for an update regarding the Youth Ambassador application.

  Public Comment: None

  5. COMMISSION REPORTS

  Commissioner Herrera shared that he was recently appointed to the PBS & KCET
  Community Advisory Board.

  Vice-Chair Goto attended the quarterly meeting of the Community Benefit
  Advisory Council of City of Hope. She also participated in the Trust for America’s
  Health Virtual Congressional Briefing on Pain in the Nation, it focused on the
  epidemics of alcohol drug and suicide deaths.

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  JULY 26, 2022
   Chair Jennings-Nuñez wanted to remind the public about opportunities to engage
  with local leaders such as Congresswoman Judy Chiu, State Senator Susan Rubio,
  and the State Assemblyman Mike Fong. She shared that Mike Fong will be hosting
  a public coffee event and Chief Harris holds monthly meetings and encouraged
  the community to interact with leaders to share any concerns.

  6. STAFF COMMENTS
  Manager Morales-Stevens provided information on the senior lunch program.

  7. ADJOURNMENT

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez adjourned the meeting at 8:35 p.m.

  Next regular meeting is tentatively scheduled in person for Tuesday, August 23, 2022 at
  6:30 p.m.

TO:  HEAR Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager

SUBJECT:  SAN GABRIEL MENTAL WELLNESS EXPO

Staff have worked diligently with Commissioners Borja, Khan and Brenhaug to develop and
finalize the details for the San Gabriel Mental Wellness Expo which is scheduled to take
place on September 187 from 12-4pm at the Grapevine Arbor. Below are the details that
have been confirmed:

The event will include workshops in English, Mandarin, and Spanish, resource booths,
activities for kids and adults and giveways. The goal of the event is to provide mental health
resources and information to residents in an inviting and enjoyable way.

Confirmed community groups include LA County Department of Mental Health, California
Phones, Chinatown Service Center, WellCare Healthplan Inc, New York Life, South Asian
Network, SGV Special Needs Group, Asian Youth Center, and YWCA San Gabriel Valley. By
offering workshops in a variety of languages and hosting diverse and engaging community
booths the hope is that the event is accessible and inviting to a wide range of individuals.

Should community members need more information about the San Gabriel Mental Wellness
Expo they are welcome to contact Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager,
at 626-308-2875 or mmoralesstevens@sgch.org.

Dear Community Leader,

The City of San Gabriel’s Human Equity, Access and Relations (HEAR) Commission is
hosting the San Gabriel Mental Wellness Expo on September 18, 2022 from 12:00pm-
4:00pm at the Grapevine Arbor. The event will consist of informational booths, giveaways,
breakout sessions, and resources.

The purpose of the HEAR Commission is to advance and advocate for equity, access,
diversity, social justice, safety, mutual appreciation, increased cultural competency,
positive inter-group relations and respect for all members of the San Gabriel community.
Collectively, the commission determined the need for additional resources and programs
specifically geared toward mental health.

In support of the event we are calling on local community organizations to take part by
hosting a community booth. The City will provide an 8’ table, 2 chairs and a canopy. We
ask that you provide information on what resources or programs your organization has
to offer and encourage you to have giveaways and/ or an interactive component to
engage the participants.

If you are interested in participating in this event, please complete the attached
application and return it via mail or email at your earliest convenience in order to reserve
your space. If you have any questions or concerns, please feel free to contact me at
mmoralesstevens@sgch.org or 626-308-2875.

Thank you in advance for your support.

Sincerely,

Matthew Morales-Stevens
Community Services Manager

  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  August 23, 2022

TO:  HEAR Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager

SUBJECT:  LAND ACKOWLEDGEMENT STATEMENT AND USES

BACKGROUND

At the October 6, 2021 meeting the Land Acknowledgement Statement (LAS) Advisory
Committee approved a purpose statement to help guide the development of the land
acknowledgment statement. The approved statement is as follows: The Land
Acknowledgement Statement serves as a clear and ongoing commitment from the City
of San Gabriel to respect and acknowledge the native peoples of San Gabriel for their
past, current, and future contributions to the region. The committee had active
discussions with the tribal leaders to ensure the language in the statement best
represented the land and peoples it was acknowledging. At the August 11, 2022 LAS
Advisory Committee approved a land acknowledgement statement and proposed uses.

PROPOSED LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT STATEMENT (LAS)

The City of San Gabriel resides on the lands of the unceded village of Sibangna and
acknowledges that the ancestors of this village and many others were collectivized at the
San Gabriel Mission. The City respectfully recognizes its responsibility to the original and
current care takers of this land, who remain an important and vibrant community. The City
strives to respect and honor the ancestral peoples’ legacy and educate residents of this
history.

POSSIBLE USES FOR THE LAS STATEMENT

The Committee has expressed interest and a need for the City’s land acknowledgement
statement to make a larger impact than simply a statement. Below is what was developed
at the May 9 meeting.
  • Post on the City Website
  • Read aloud at City meetings and functions
   Land Acknowledgement Statement and Uses
  August 23, 2022
  Page 2

  •  Post at the front of the Mission Playhouse and/ or City Hall
  •  Map of the indigenous villages with the statement
  •  Recommend the San Gabriel Unified School District use the statement at events
  and include it in the California history class curriculum
  •  Initiation of education and outreach

STAFF RECCOMENDATION

Staff recommends that the HEAR Commission approve the statement and proposed uses
or send it back to the committee for revision with proposed amendments. The statement
and uses will also be presented to the Historic Preservation and Cultural Resource
Commission. Upon both commission’s approval staff will present it to the tribal leaders
followed by the City Council.
